answers.q1_what_did_you_play: Jumpy Dumpty for 2, then Kaboom! for 1, spending all 3 Energy on the only enemy. Jumpy Dumpty's two 8-damage hits both have to land on the Fuzzy Wurm Crawler since it is the only target, so that is 16 plus a Bomb sitting on the board for 6 more; Kaboom! adds 7 on top. That is 23 damage this turn and 6 banked, taking the Crawler from 46 to 23 with the Bomb still pending. I did not touch Spark Knight's Oath or Duck and Cover.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: I weighed Spark Knight's Oath first and rejected it on arithmetic. Oath costs 2 of my 3 Energy and then routes Attacks through the Spark bank at 3 Spark each — with exactly 3 Spark I can pay for exactly one Attack, so the whole turn becomes Oath plus Kaboom! for 7 damage with 1 Energy left over for Duck and Cover. Jumpy Dumpty is printed as an Elemental Skill, so Oath does not discount it and the leftover Energy cannot cast it. Oath is a card that wants a Spark bank bigger than one Attack's worth and a hand that is mostly Attacks; this turn it is neither, and it costs 16 damage to set up. I also glanced at Kaboom! plus Duck and Cover for 7 damage and 5 Block with an Energy floating, which is strictly worse than the line I took against a 4-damage swing.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: All defense and all setup. I take the full 4 to the face and go to 38/62, and Duck and Cover would have absorbed it outright. I also gave up establishing Oath, so if the next turns hand me a wall of Attacks and Sparks keep accruing, I am paying full Energy for them instead of having the discount already down. And I dumped the Bomb now rather than saving Jumpy Dumpty for a board where its random targeting has more bodies to spread across.
answers.q4_different_intent: Yes. At 4 damage the Block is worth less than a fifth of the damage I gain by ignoring it, so it is not close. If the Crawler had telegraphed something in the high teens or above — enough that eating it threatened my 42 HP over the next couple of turns, or enough that 5 Block was a meaningful fraction of it — I would have cut Kaboom! and played Jumpy Dumpty plus Duck and Cover, keeping 16 plus the Bomb while blunting the hit. A telegraphed defensive or buffing intent instead of an attack would have made Oath tempting, since a turn where I take nothing is the cheapest turn to spend on setup.
